## Analysis

Relative dilation failed to improve the 473-element plateau, so equal-source affine unions are now exhausted across translation, reflection, copy count, and scale. Deletion, direct-coordinate, and spare-capacity searches also stalled, showing the incumbent’s advantage depends on global collision structure that local moves readily destroy. The successful lineage came from nonlinear tensor projection, suggesting the next useful transformation should globally refold coordinates rather than rearrange copies. Quotient–remainder refolding has not been tested and can systematically merge or separate entire families of sums and differences.
